requirement_text: Users must complete creation, first use, revision, hosting, and recovery without seeing a source tree, shell command, raw stack trace, branch, deployment configuration, or model-provider setup.
primary_task_title: Spore desktop and web builder shell

requirement_text: Technical details may be available through a support disclosure or downloadable diagnostic bundle. They are never the only explanation or recovery action.
primary_task_title: Spore desktop and web builder shell

requirement_text: The conversation accepts text, file and image attachments, screen selection, and optional voice input. A text equivalent remains available for every voice operation.
primary_task_title: Conversational build and operating experience

requirement_text: Progress describes work such as "Checking appointment conflicts" or "Preparing your update." Show elapsed time, queued/running state, cancellation, and when user input is needed. Do not invent completion percentages or precise time estimates without evidence.
primary_task_title: Isolated previews and test datasets

requirement_text: Stop cancels pending work and cooperatively ends running work. It distinguishes a cancelled build, an external action already committed, and a release already installed. The conversation remains recoverable.
primary_task_title: Conversational build and operating experience

requirement_text: Mid-build feedback is acknowledged immediately. Changes apply at a recorded safe boundary or become a queued revision. Spore states which request the candidate implements and never silently drops steering.
primary_task_title: App planning generation and change reconciliation

requirement_text: Generated apps and Spore surfaces support keyboard navigation, visible focus, screen readers, reduced motion, text scaling, and responsive layouts. WCAG 2.2 AA is the proposed acceptance target for applicable web interfaces; automated checks are supplemented by manual task testing.
primary_task_title: Spore desktop and web builder shell

requirement_text: Formatting respects locale, currency, time zone, and daylight-saving behavior. The app brief records business time-zone rules. The interface is localization-ready; English is the launch support language unless the decision register expands it.
primary_task_title: Generated app design system and visual iteration

requirement_text: The Spore builder itself has tested desktop and web account, library, conversation, preview, and administration flows. Desktop installs and file access use an explicit device handoff from the web builder. A browser-only session cannot silently install software, read local folders, or guarantee permanent browser storage. Web/PWA clients explain browser storage eviction and sync status; a standalone durable local desktop app is a distinct distribution target.
primary_task_title: Device enrollment and web desktop handoff

requirement_text: Creation assigns an immutable app ID, owner, source lineage, data namespace, and conversation namespace. Renaming cannot change identity, invalidate links, or create a different update channel.
primary_task_title: Freeze shared contracts and compatibility rules

requirement_text: Every app has a durable, versioned brief containing its purpose, users, workflows, data entities, access rules, supported devices, integrations, visual direction, acceptance scenarios, and decisions. The brief is maintained as the app changes and is distinct from the raw transcript.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: Spore generates a complete working application: interface, business logic, validation, storage access, error states, empty states, loading states, and required documentation for the owner. Placeholder buttons and hard-coded successful results do not satisfy a workflow.
primary_task_title: App planning generation and change reconciliation

requirement_text: Builds use a supported application contract: web interface, controlled server functions, typed data access, migrations, capability declarations, and verification scenarios. The generator can create custom layouts and logic; it is not limited to selecting prewritten templates.
primary_task_title: Freeze shared contracts and compatibility rules

requirement_text: Uploads are scanned and parsed in isolation. Instructions found in documents, imported records, websites, or screenshots cannot grant agent permissions. Import analysis previews mappings, rejected rows, duplicates, relationships, and dates before production writes.
primary_task_title: Public runtime APIs uploads and data isolation

requirement_text: The owner can duplicate an app, choose whether to include data, and obtain a new app identity. Credentials and external-action grants are never copied automatically. Duplication does not make the new app an update recipient of the original.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: Archive preserves the app and records without consuming active build resources. Delete explains the separate effects on source, installed apps, hosted data, backups, and other users. Destructive deletion requires owner authorization and a recoverable retention interval where applicable.
primary_task_title: Import export retention and deletion

requirement_text: An app can be exported with source, lockfiles, assets, schema, migration history, build instructions, runtime compatibility metadata, and license notices. Data export is a separate selection. Secrets and platform signing keys are excluded; connection reconnection instructions are included.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: Conversion between local and hosted storage is a managed migration with validation and a recovery checkpoint. Converting a shared app to a standalone local copy explicitly explains that the copy stops sharing data and receiving business-wide changes.
primary_task_title: Migration planning rehearsal and write fencing

requirement_text: The application contract includes an editable theme, layout, navigation, visual assets, and reusable accessible components. Users can request substantial visual redesigns through chat, supply brand references, and obtain generated image assets when needed. Asset generation consumes the disclosed build budget, retains provenance and usage rights metadata, and never requires an image-provider account from the user.
primary_task_title: Generated app design system and visual iteration

requirement_text: Every maintained app has a recoverable source capsule containing the approved source, brief, dependency lockfile, asset provenance, migration history, and build/runtime recipe. A creator's private local vault or verified owner export can hold it; it is never included in member/public packages. Cloud archival cannot delete the last recoverable capsule without explicit owner deletion. At cloud capacity, stop new billable storage or request an export/capacity choice; do not disable installed local apps. Reimporting a capsule validates provenance and ownership and restores the app's maintenance context without replaying old jobs or grants.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: Archive, pause hosting, cancel a subscription, uninstall, and delete are distinct operations. Archiving hides an app and stops new builds; it does not silently stop production hosting or erase data. A business ownership transfer verifies both parties, billing responsibility, data access, active builds, signing/update identity, and connection ownership before committing. Private apps are shared through authenticated invitations or expiring installation links; downloading a package alone grants no hosted-data or builder access.
primary_task_title: Source archival app lifecycle and ownership transfer

requirement_text: "Show unpaid deposits" is an application operation. "Add deposit reminders" is a software change. Ambiguous requests are clarified before a consequential action.
primary_task_title: Conversational build and operating experience

requirement_text: App operations use the same server-enforced record and action permissions as the normal interface. A chat answer cannot reveal information the user cannot otherwise access.
primary_task_title: Trusted data authorization and policy cache

requirement_text: Build and publication permissions are app-specific. A member's suggestion becomes an owner-visible request; it does not modify source or initiate paid inference beyond the allowed feedback path.
primary_task_title: Trusted data authorization and policy cache

requirement_text: Development history, source, diagnostics, and build costs are private to authorized builders. Customer-facing chat cannot retrieve them through prompt injection or direct API calls.
primary_task_title: Trusted data authorization and policy cache

requirement_text: Sending messages, deleting business records, changing access, making purchases, and modifying connected external systems require suitable action grants. Repeated authorized workflows can use scoped standing grants with visible revocation.
primary_task_title: Tools capabilities and mutation policy

requirement_text: The agent uses authenticated, short-lived app-scoped capabilities. Generated code and user prompts cannot escalate them. Authorization is rechecked at execution and publication, including after a role is revoked mid-build.
primary_task_title: Tools capabilities and mutation policy

requirement_text: Owners can disable operational AI for members while retaining the owner's development chat. Runtime AI consumption and app-building consumption have separate budgets and usage records.
primary_task_title: Model gateway and auxiliary inference

requirement_text: Installed apps retain Ask Spore without requiring the full builder window to be open. An authenticated owner can resume from another supported device. A platform outage leaves local non-AI app functions available.
primary_task_title: Embedded chat and update review in generated apps

requirement_text: Owner development conversations and member operational conversations use separate contexts and data retrieval policies even when presented through one chat entry point. Switching between operating and changing the app is visible and authority-checked. Service outage or entitlement expiry leaves an explanation and durable unsent draft/feedback option rather than a dead composer or a falsely accepted cloud request.
primary_task_title: Conversational build and operating experience

requirement_text: The service records an accepted change request before enqueueing work. Admission is idempotent: retries after a lost response do not create duplicate builds, charges, hosted resources, or releases.
primary_task_title: Durable change requests and execution coordination

requirement_text: Each build captures the request revision, source revision, app brief revision, runtime version, dependency lockfile, tool/model configuration, authorization, and budget. The same identifiers connect progress, diagnostics, artifacts, and accounting.
primary_task_title: Durable change requests and execution coordination

requirement_text: Build execution is isolated from production, other customers, platform credentials, and signing infrastructure. Dependency installation, generated tests, and generated server code are treated as untrusted execution, not protected merely by an Electron renderer sandbox.
primary_task_title: Tools capabilities and mutation policy

requirement_text: The controlled pipeline performs request analysis, planning, implementation, dependency resolution, static checks, functional tests, browser checks, security checks, migration rehearsal, packaging, and release preparation. Required stages cannot be skipped because the model says it succeeded.
primary_task_title: Extract and integrate the shared agent engine

requirement_text: Acceptance scenarios originate from the user's brief and preserved business rules. A separate verification context evaluates them. Builder-authored tests provide additional evidence but cannot alone determine readiness.
primary_task_title: Independent verification and release evidence

requirement_text: Verification covers empty and realistic datasets, access denial, validation, error recovery, mobile layouts, accessibility, and existing critical workflows. A screenshot or page-load check alone does not establish functional completion.
primary_task_title: Independent verification and release evidence

requirement_text: Durable checkpoints support retries, infrastructure restarts, cancellation, and continuation with preserved budgets. A restart cannot refill a repair or spending allowance. Infrastructure failures and implementation failures have distinct retry policies.
primary_task_title: Extract and integrate the shared agent engine

requirement_text: Multiple conversations can propose changes, but publication is serialized per app. A candidate built from an obsolete release must be reconciled and reverified against the current source and schema before publication. Users never resolve Git conflicts manually.
primary_task_title: Durable change requests and execution coordination

requirement_text: Cloud builds continue when the owner's device closes. An owner-selectable local build route also ships under the same job, budget, and verification contracts; choosing it is optional for the user, not optional implementation work. It uses automatically managed tooling and service model access without requiring a local model server. Local execution may pause when the device sleeps and must accurately report that state. If a certified local sandbox cannot start, offer cloud execution with explicit source/data-transfer consent; do not silently run unsandboxed or upload the project. OS-specific signing can still require a remote signing worker even when implementation runs locally; explain that dependency before starting.
primary_task_title: Disposable cloud build workers

requirement_text: A job has bounded execution time, dependency size, disk, memory, network access, child processes, repair attempts, and inference spend. Proposed default: a 45-minute active build deadline with three automatic code-repair attempts. Longer work is checkpointed and requires an explicit budget extension.
primary_task_title: Durable change requests and execution coordination

requirement_text: Browser and external-service verification uses test credentials and non-production side effects. Spore never sends real customers test emails, books actual appointments, or initiates real payments merely to check a generated workflow.
primary_task_title: Independent verification and release evidence

requirement_text: Failure preserves useful work, identifies the failing stage, and offers a meaningful next action. Users can resume, change the request, restore the previous candidate, or request support without editing internal directories.
primary_task_title: App planning generation and change reconciliation

requirement_text: Model routing, context compaction, asset generation, voice processing, and fallback preserve the app's data-processing policy and recorded spending authorization. Fallback to a different provider or region requires compatible consent and contractual processing settings. A model/dependency/runtime upgrade triggers regression evaluation before becoming a default; cost or quota failure cannot silently select a lower quality path and claim equivalent verification.
primary_task_title: Model gateway and auxiliary inference

requirement_text: Every packaged app has its own name, icon, stable application identity, data directory, installer, and update channel. It launches into the app rather than the Spore library.
primary_task_title: Reproducible packaging and isolated signing

requirement_text: The package contains the application, supported runtime, capability bridge, embedded chat client, and update/recovery client. It does not contain a complete duplicate development environment, provider secrets, source history, or platform administration credentials.
primary_task_title: Reproducible packaging and isolated signing

requirement_text: Installing and using a local app requires no Git, Node.js, package manager, browser driver, or model-server installation. Build tooling is provisioned by Spore in a controlled environment.
primary_task_title: Managed local build execution

requirement_text: Launch supports Windows x64, macOS arm64 and x64, and Linux x64 through explicitly tested installer formats. Proposed formats are Windows installer, signed/notarized macOS installer distribution, and Linux AppImage with a verified update path. Exact minimum OS versions are frozen before the release test matrix is executed; platform support cannot be inferred from source compilation.
primary_task_title: Close product vendor and platform decisions

requirement_text: Desktop capabilities include owner-approved file open/save, printing, notifications, clipboard use, and selected-folder access. Each capability is mediated by a trusted broker and declared in the release. New capabilities trigger review. Arbitrary filesystem and shell access are not generated-app defaults.
primary_task_title: Native capabilities and restricted generated logic

requirement_text: Packages and release metadata have verifiable provenance. Signing happens after verification in infrastructure inaccessible to generated code. Owners do not supply code-signing certificates for ordinary Spore distribution.
primary_task_title: Reproducible packaging and isolated signing

requirement_text: Uninstalling an app clearly distinguishes application files from retained local data. Reinstallation with the same identity recovers retained data safely. Installing a duplicate app cannot silently adopt another app's data.
primary_task_title: Branded desktop hosts and local application lifecycle

requirement_text: Installed apps keep operating if the Spore builder is removed. Subscription cancellation removes paid build/service entitlements according to the billing policy, not the ability to open local records.
primary_task_title: Branded desktop hosts and local application lifecycle

requirement_text: The installed app uses a stable, signed Spore host plus independently signed, immutable app bundles stored outside the signed host installation. Only the trusted host verifies and activates bundles; generated code cannot change trust roots or its bundle directory. Host security updates require no model-driven app rebuild and can be delivered without a build subscription. Each app still has a distinct signed installer, identity, and data directory. Platform signing/update constraints must be proven with this exact design before freezing packaging; a design revision must preserve independent host patching and app identity.
primary_task_title: Prove signed host and bundle update design

requirement_text: Local app data, private source capsules, OS credentials, and cached shared-app records have different access and encryption rules. Device enrollment, app linking, sign-out, multiple OS users, lost-device revocation, and local account recovery are tested. Standalone personal app access does not require a paid license check; business-managed cached data remains subject to access-expiry policy. Owner-requested deletion cannot be guaranteed on an offline or unmanaged device, which is stated accurately.
primary_task_title: Device enrollment and web desktop handoff

requirement_text: An immutable release manifest binds app ID, publisher, source revision, artifact hashes, platform/architecture, runtime compatibility, schema compatibility, permissions, acceptance evidence, and migration plan. The publication decision binds the exact reviewed manifest.
primary_task_title: Independent verification and release evidence

requirement_text: Updates download and stage while the app is running. Installation occurs at a safe point, after unsaved work is preserved and the user is notified. Maintenance windows and an opt-in automatic update policy are available.
primary_task_title: Host and app update delivery with recovery

requirement_text: Update clients verify identity, signature, integrity, compatibility, and authorized channel before activation. They reject tampered files, another app's artifact, and unauthorized rollback/replay of old releases.
primary_task_title: Prove signed host and bundle update design

requirement_text: Interrupted download, disk exhaustion, process crash, power loss, and startup failure have tested recovery behavior. A known working runtime and an installation journal remain available until the new release passes health checks.
primary_task_title: Host and app update delivery with recovery

requirement_text: Application releases and the shared Spore runtime have separate version lifecycles. A compatibility matrix prevents a runtime update from breaking installed apps or a generated app from using unsupported APIs.
primary_task_title: Prove signed host and bundle update design

requirement_text: Local migrations take a validated backup or transactional checkpoint before mutation. Hosted migrations rehearse on an isolated dataset with equivalent structure and representative scale. Destructive changes require a specific approval that describes affected data.
primary_task_title: Prove backend recovery and migration semantics

requirement_text: Prefer additive schema changes and bounded compatibility windows for old and new clients. A hosted API must not silently break devices that have not updated. Clients below a required minimum version receive a recoverable upgrade screen without discarding pending data.
primary_task_title: Migration planning rehearsal and write fencing

requirement_text: Code rollback and data recovery are separate operations. Automatic rollback is permitted only when the manifest establishes schema compatibility. Otherwise Spore uses a verified forward repair or a coordinated restore with explicit handling of writes since the recovery point.
primary_task_title: Migration planning rehearsal and write fencing

requirement_text: A restore that would discard newer business records shows the recovery time and affected writes and requires owner authorization. The service must never describe a lossy restore as a transparent undo.
primary_task_title: Migration planning rehearsal and write fencing

requirement_text: Hosted publication uses a candidate environment, readiness checks, controlled traffic activation, and monitored health. Database changes and queued jobs have compatible transition rules. Only one release coordinator can advance an app's active version.
primary_task_title: Immutable release manifests and approval authority

requirement_text: A withdrawn release stops new offers and supports an emergency repair path. Signing-key rotation and revocation are operational procedures tested before launch.
primary_task_title: Host and app update delivery with recovery

requirement_text: Notifications distinguish "ready to review," "published," "installed on this device," and "action needed." Owners can inspect other devices' versions without receiving a notification for every routine background stage.
primary_task_title: Transactional email and product notifications

requirement_text: Desktop app bundles, the signed host, hosted APIs, schema, sync protocol, and web service-worker caches have an explicit compatibility matrix. Proposed online protocol support is the current and previous protocol major for at least 90 days; long-disconnected clients preserve pending operations and follow DATA-14. Web/PWA activation must not combine new UI code with incompatible cached assets or discard unsent work. Supported host major versions receive critical security patches for at least 12 months after supersession, with 90 days' end-of-support notice; these targets require D-11 approval and operating-cost validation.
primary_task_title: Freeze shared contracts and compatibility rules

requirement_text: A release's permitted environments and target platforms are declared before approval. Approved artifacts must exist and pass checks for every selected target before a coordinated publication. A single-platform packaging failure cannot silently publish a partial multi-platform release. Activation maintenance requires a backup, drain/fence of relevant writes and jobs, a maximum duration, and a tested abort path. Automatic publication policies never waive a new capability or destructive migration approval.
primary_task_title: Migration planning rehearsal and write fencing

requirement_text: Spore provisions and operates compute, a fresh logical database, object storage, authentication configuration, secrets, jobs, logs, and a default HTTPS app URL. Users do not need a cloud account.
primary_task_title: Managed backend provisioning

requirement_text: Provisioning is a durable state machine with idempotent resource creation, resource ownership tags, quotas, readiness checks, cancellation handling, and orphan cleanup. A partial failure must not produce an indefinitely billed, undiscoverable app.
primary_task_title: Managed backend provisioning

requirement_text: Each app has separated production and preview resources. Preview deployments cannot use production credentials, mutate production records, or send production communications by default. Preview environments expire and release billable resources.
primary_task_title: Isolated previews and test datasets

requirement_text: Generated apps support CRUD workflows, relationships, validation, indexed search, reports, uploads, background tasks, schedules, webhooks, and transactional notifications through supported service interfaces. Long-running work uses job workers rather than blocking ordinary requests.
primary_task_title: Typed local and hosted app data runtime

requirement_text: Owners can invite members, assign access, revoke sessions, and configure public/customer-facing routes. Backend access checks are enforced independently of client UI visibility. Private apps are the default.
primary_task_title: Accounts businesses apps and membership

requirement_text: Hosted apps have a default Spore subdomain and support custom domains with guided ownership verification, certificate issuance, renewal, and failure recovery. Domain purchase is not included in the subscription. DNS changes may require user action with the domain provider.
primary_task_title: Domains private origins and public routing

requirement_text: Per-app resource limits cover requests, CPU, database operations and storage, object storage, transfer, authentication use, messaging, scheduled jobs, and runtime AI. Limits are enforced on the service side and cannot be bypassed by calling a provider endpoint directly.
primary_task_title: Validate economics capacity and support obligations

requirement_text: A problematic app cannot exhaust another customer's capacity. Platform and tenant quotas, concurrency controls, circuit breakers, and outbound network policies apply before expensive work.
primary_task_title: Managed backend provisioning

requirement_text: Hosted app identity survives renaming, domain changes, owner-device changes, and redeployment. Resource reassignment checks ownership rather than relying on names or URLs.
primary_task_title: Accounts businesses apps and membership

requirement_text: Owners can pause hosting, export data, restore a backup, and remove a hosted app through chat or app settings. Pausing explains what staff and customers experience and which resources remain billable.
primary_task_title: Source archival app lifecycle and ownership transfer

requirement_text: Private previews and downloads require independent, expiring access grants and use origins isolated from the builder and production. Custom-domain removal/reassignment verifies ownership and prevents stale routing takeover. Public pages do not receive builder cookies, tokens, or source access; domain changes preserve canonical app identity and require tested OAuth redirect behavior.
primary_task_title: Device enrollment and web desktop handoff

requirement_text: An app's runtime need for a connector broker, scheduled cloud job, authentication, AI, or hosted data is recorded separately from build-time cloud use. A purely local app may use owner-initiated paid runtime services without occupying a hosted-app slot; persistent shared endpoints, cloud schedules, or shared databases require that slot. Creation and changes explain both entitlement and offline implications before committing resources.
primary_task_title: Managed backend provisioning

requirement_text: Spore accounts, generated-app user accounts, and third-party service connections are distinct identities with separate grants. Signing into a generated app never grants access to the Spore builder.
primary_task_title: Accounts businesses apps and membership

requirement_text: Launch supports managed email sign-in and Google and Microsoft sign-in for generated apps, including invite-only access, recovery, session expiry, and session revocation. Provider configuration and production verification are completed by Spore where a platform-owned integration is used.
primary_task_title: Managed sign-in and account security

requirement_text: OAuth connection flows use maintained protocols and components with server-side token storage, redirect validation, anti-forgery protection, least-privilege scopes, refresh handling, and disconnect/revocation. Generated code never implements password storage or receives platform master credentials.
primary_task_title: Managed sign-in and account security

requirement_text: Provider consent, organization restrictions, and provider verification requirements remain visible when they require user action. Spore must not claim a connection is complete until it has tested the required permissions.
primary_task_title: Managed sign-in and account security

requirement_text: Launch connector families cover Google Calendar/Drive/Sheets, Microsoft calendar/mail/files, transactional email, generic authenticated HTTP APIs, and incoming/outgoing webhooks. Each advertised action has a tested connection, execution, revocation, and failure contract. Customer-organization policy can restrict available connectors.
primary_task_title: Google business connectors

requirement_text: Business-side payment collection, when requested by an app, uses a connected payment provider's hosted checkout and test environment. Merchant onboarding and fees belong to the business and provider; Spore does not store card numbers. This does not create an app-resale marketplace.
primary_task_title: Connected merchant checkout

requirement_text: Recurring external actions have explicit schedules, idempotency rules, recipient scopes, spending limits where relevant, and an audit trail. Disconnecting an account disables dependent jobs and informs the owner without losing app data.
primary_task_title: Durable jobs schedules and effect receipts

requirement_text: Generated code cannot bypass record, field, file, or action policy by using a raw database credential or by declaring itself an administrator. A trusted data/capability service checks the end-user or narrowly scoped job principal on every operation. Generated queries and custom functions use that broker; privileged migrations execute only under the reviewed release service. Export, search, counts, joins, and attachments must not become indirect data leaks.
primary_task_title: Trusted data authorization and policy cache

requirement_text: Each connector action declares read/write scope, safe retry policy, idempotency support, timeouts, rate limits, reconciliation, and consent requirements. Where a provider cannot deduplicate or confirm an action after a lost response, mark the outcome uncertain and stop automatic retries until reconciled. Do not promise exactly-once external side effects without a provider-supported mechanism. Schedules specify business time zone, daylight-saving policy, missed-run behavior, overlap, bounded retries, and a dead-letter recovery path.
primary_task_title: Durable jobs schedules and effect receipts

requirement_text: Connection revocation propagates to runtime and queued work within five minutes under healthy connectivity. Generated-app sessions, Spore builder sessions, connector tokens, and cached authorization have separately tested revocation bounds. Identity linking cannot merge two accounts solely because unverified emails match. Notification services handle verified senders, bounces, complaints, recipient consent, and abuse controls; public feedback cannot trigger unbounded paid inference.
primary_task_title: Managed sign-in and account security

requirement_text: The app owner controls application records and authorized exports. Spore keeps customer data, source, transcripts, and service metadata in distinct stores with separate access and retention policies.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: A local app uses local durable storage by default. Cloud backup and cloud development disclose what leaves the device. Source and explicitly selected diagnostic samples can be sent for a build without uploading the entire live database.
primary_task_title: App source vault brief and legacy import

requirement_text: Shared apps have a server-authoritative record model with scoped device caches. Offline-capable workflows show which changes are saved locally, awaiting synchronization, rejected, or conflicted.
primary_task_title: Offline storage synchronization and conflicts

requirement_text: Synchronization uses stable record IDs, operation IDs, versions, deletion markers, and idempotent retries. Concurrent changes cannot silently overwrite another person's work. Merge policies are defined per entity; unresolved conflicts have a human-readable choice.
primary_task_title: Offline storage synchronization and conflicts

requirement_text: Workflows requiring global uniqueness or immediate authority, such as scarce appointment slots or payment confirmation, cannot promise final success offline. They show a pending state until the server accepts the operation.
primary_task_title: Typed local and hosted app data runtime

requirement_text: Revoked users lose online access immediately after the configured revocation propagation bound. Offline cached information cannot be remotely guaranteed erased from a disconnected device; sensitive apps must support disabling offline storage or requiring expiring online access. This limitation is explained at policy configuration.
primary_task_title: Offline storage synchronization and conflicts

requirement_text: Data export includes structured records, attachments, relationship keys, schema descriptions, and time-zone metadata in documented formats. It is available without an active build subscription during the retention window.
primary_task_title: Import export retention and deletion

requirement_text: Import and local-to-hosted migration validate counts, relationships, rejected records, and checksums where applicable. Interrupted transfers resume without duplicating business records.
primary_task_title: Import export retention and deletion

requirement_text: Backups are encrypted, access-controlled, monitored, and periodically restored in isolation. Proposed defaults: 30 days of daily recovery points plus a journal or incremental snapshot mechanism with no more than a 15-minute recovery gap for hosted data, recovery points before every schema migration, and a four-hour recovery-time objective for the included size envelope. Database rows, referenced objects, sync cursors, and encryption-key references form a consistent recoverable set. Daily snapshots alone do not satisfy the recovery-point objective. These are launch test targets, not assumptions about a selected provider.
primary_task_title: Prove backend recovery and migration semantics

requirement_text: Local apps create migration recovery points and support user-controlled export plus opt-in managed backup. Backup failures are visible; a local device failure cannot be presented as recoverable unless a usable off-device backup exists.
primary_task_title: Consistent backup and incremental recovery storage

requirement_text: Preview datasets are synthetic or explicitly approved, minimized copies. Data masking protects sensitive fields where possible. Production secrets never enter test snapshots.
primary_task_title: Isolated previews and test datasets

requirement_text: Account and app deletion specify retention, backup expiry, legal retention exceptions where applicable, and completion status. Deleted material is not reintroduced by restoring a stale backup without applying deletion records.
primary_task_title: Import export retention and deletion

requirement_text: A hosted restore creates a new recovery epoch and fences old clients and job workers. Reconcile acknowledged writes, object versions, deletion records, and outbox receipts before reopening writes. Old offline operations are quarantined for migration or owner review, not replayed blindly. Restoring app records must not resend emails, replay payments, reverse membership revocation, or restore expired external grants. Operator disaster recovery follows the same invariants.
primary_task_title: Prove backend recovery and migration semantics

requirement_text: Proposed offline incremental-sync window is 30 days. Tombstone and operation retention cover that window plus a seven-day safety margin. Older devices perform an authenticated resnapshot; pending local edits are exported or transformed through an explicit reconciliation path before any cache replacement. Schema migration preserves the local pending-operation queue and can reject incompatible edits without deleting them. No indefinitely disconnected client blocks server cleanup forever.
primary_task_title: Offline storage synchronization and conflicts

requirement_text: Publish and enforce a retention schedule for source capsules, raw transcripts, attachments, audit events, backups, usage records, exports, revoked credentials, and expired previews. Proposed defaults are 30 days for downloadable export links, 90 days for detailed technical logs with secret redaction, and one year for security audit events; source/current app records remain while the account/app is maintained. Billing/statutory exceptions and account-deletion behavior require D-06 review. Limits never silently erase the last recoverable app source or required legal/audit evidence.
primary_task_title: Consistent backup and incremental recovery storage

requirement_text: Show warnings at 70%, 90%, and 100% of a resource allowance. Owners can purchase capacity or authorize a capped overage. An agent cannot approve its own spending increase.
primary_task_title: Validate economics capacity and support obligations

requirement_text: At a hard limit, reject the affected new billable operation with a recoverable explanation. Never truncate records, partially acknowledge a write, or delete data to fit a plan. Owner administration and export have a separate protected access path.
primary_task_title: Runtime quotas isolation and outage policy

requirement_text: An accepted build reserves a budget before work begins, reconciles actual usage, and releases unused reservation on settlement. Duplicate provider events and payment webhooks cannot double-charge.
primary_task_title: Usage reservations and settlement ledger

requirement_text: Payment, entitlement, resource usage, and app state remain reconcilable after a service restart or missed webhook. A completed checkout with a delayed webhook can be recovered without asking the user to pay again.
primary_task_title: Plans subscriptions and entitlement model

requirement_text: Voluntary cancellation keeps paid features until the paid-through date, then suspends hosting and new builds. Failed renewal instead receives seven days of payment-recovery grace before suspension. Both paths retain hosted data and owner export access for 30 days after suspension before scheduled deletion with advance notices. Local non-service functions continue.
